hints: Focus on where Na, Mg, Al and Si sit in the Periodic Table, they are all in the same period from left to right.
Recall how atomic radius changes across Period 3, so Na is the largest atom and Si is the smallest.
Now link that to electronegativity, as atoms get smaller across the period they pull bonding electrons more strongly, so the smallest atom should be highest up.
walkthrough:
**Place the elements in order**

Great start, let's get organised. Na, Mg, Al and Si are the first four elements of Period 3, in that left to right order.

Order across period: $\text{Na} \rightarrow \text{Mg} \rightarrow \text{Al} \rightarrow \text{Si}$

**Predict the atomic radius trend**

Across a period, proton number increases but electrons are added to the same shell, so shielding stays similar.

Greater nuclear charge pulls the outer shell in more strongly, so radius decreases: $\text{Na} > \text{Mg} > \text{Al} > \text{Si}$. On the x-axis, Na must be furthest right and Si furthest left.

**Predict the electronegativity trend**

Electronegativity is the power to attract bonding electrons. Smaller atoms with higher nuclear charge attract more strongly.

So electronegativity increases across the period: $\text{Si} > \text{Al} > \text{Mg} > \text{Na}$. On the y-axis, Si must be highest and Na lowest.

**Combine both trends**

We need a falling pattern from top-left to bottom-right. Small radius, high electronegativity at the top-left (Si), large radius, low electronegativity at the bottom-right (Na), with Al then Mg in between in order.

options.A: Incorrect. It puts Na at large radius and low electronegativity which is right, but it puts Si at low electronegativity and Al as the highest. In reality Si is the most electronegative and has the smallest radius of the four.
options.B: Correct. Si is top-left (smallest radius, highest electronegativity), then Al, then Mg, then Na bottom-right (largest radius, lowest electronegativity). This perfectly matches both trends: radius Na > Mg > Al > Si and electronegativity Si > Al > Mg > Na.
options.C: Incorrect. This shows electronegativity increasing as atomic radius increases, with Na highest. This is the opposite of the true relationship. Larger atoms hold electrons less tightly, so Na should be lowest, not highest.
options.D: Incorrect. Although it has the correct vertical order for electronegativity (Si top, Na bottom), the horizontal order is wrong. It shows Al with a smaller atomic radius than Si, but Si comes later in the period so Si must be smaller than Al.
